replacements.after: Prioritize October RHC telehealth claims reconciliation and Medicaid financing exposure. CMS's non-behavioral distant-site billing change took effect October 1, 2026, with systems implementation October 5. Provider-tax statutory changes already have effective dates; CMS-2452-P proposes implementing rules, so do not treat all exposure as contingent on finalization. replacements.before: CMS published NPRM CMS‑2452‑P to amend the indirect hold-harmless threshold for health-care-related taxes and related reporting. The proposal ties permissible tax thresholds to taxes imposed as of July 4, 2025 and phases down thresholds in certain states beginning FFY 2028.
replacements.after: Section 71115 of Public Law 119-21 establishes statutory provider-tax limits effective October 1, 2026, and a phase-down for expansion states beginning federal fiscal year 2028. CMS-2452-P, published in July, proposes implementing definitions, calculations and reporting requirements. Distinguish these proposed regulations from the statutory changes they implement.

replacements.before: If finalized as proposed, state supplemental-payment constructs that depend on provider taxes could be reduced or restructured. Facility-level revenue tied to supplemental payments and provider-tax mechanisms is planning-risk exposure; hospitals should isolate these revenue streams in downside models and obtain written OHCA guidance before changing operating forecasts.
replacements.after: Do not assume statutory exposure waits for final regulations. Identify revenue supported by provider-tax-funded supplemental payments and seek OHCA guidance on Oklahoma's applicable tax classes and transition provisions before estimating facility-level effects.

replacements.before: CMS proposed rule CMS‑2452‑P would amend the indirect hold-harmless threshold for health-care-related taxes and change reporting and calculation rules; facility exposure depends on the final rule and state responses.
replacements.after: Statutory provider-tax changes have effective dates independent of CMS-2452-P, which proposes implementing definitions, calculations and reporting. CMS identifies October 1, 2026 for new statutory thresholds and a phase-down for expansion states beginning October 1, 2027, federal fiscal year 2028.

replacements.before: Until CMS finalizes the rule and Oklahoma publishes implementation choices, hospitals should isolate provider-tax-funded supplemental payments in downside models and seek written OHCA guidance before rebasing budgets.
replacements.after: Separate existing law from proposed implementation details in financial scenarios. Obtain Oklahoma-specific guidance before estimating hospital-level effects; the retained national sources do not establish a particular facility revenue reduction.
